part.text:
Fixed. The bug: when a memoized component bails out of re-rendering, `reorderChildren` walks its copied child tree to re-place host DOM nodes, but the recursive call for nested function components discarded the returned `oldDom` cursor — so nested children were placed relative to a stale DOM position, scrambling sibling order.

Changes in src/clone-element.js:
- `ChildOrder.prototype.reorderChildren` (src/clone-element.js:89): reassign `oldDom = this.reorderChildren(walk, oldDom)` so the DOM insertion cursor advances past nested component subtrees (mirrors upstream preactjs/preact#2896).
- Added the `childVNode._children != null` guard in `diffChildren` (src/clone-element.js:267) matching the same upstream change (protects against suspended children).

Validation:
- `compat/test/browser/memo.test.js` — all 9 tests pass, including `should not unnecessarily reorder children #2895`, which fails on the unpatched baseline (`<li>C,D,A,B` vs expected `<li>A,B,C,D`).
- Full karma suite: everything passes except one pre-existing headless-Chrome focus failure in `events.test.js` that also fails on the unpatched baseline.
- `mocha test/shared test/node` (27 tests) and eslint are clean.
